title: Jensen Huang considers returning to Nvidia CEO role as allies build war room to lobby board

content_html:
On November 16, the Financial Times reported that Jensen Huang is considering returning to the CEO position at Nvidia, and supporters in Silicon Valley’s tech community have begun pressuring Nvidia’s board to reinstate him.

The report said Huang has discussed a possible comeback with close associates. One ally said supporters are building a “war room” made up of Silicon Valley executives to lobby the board to support his return, and plan to seek support from the White House. The person said Huang himself supports these efforts and that, in the tech world, almost every influential figure apart from the frontier AI labs likes Huang.

Over the past weekend, the wave of support kept growing. Corporate executives including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney backed an open letter calling on the board to “Bring Jensen Back”; since Huang resigned, several Nvidia employees have also publicly called for his return and signed the letter.

However, the path back to his job faces resistance. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that after Huang’s departure, Nvidia’s leadership needs a “major shake-up.” At the same time, Huang does not hold enough shares to control the company and cannot overturn the board’s decision. Currently, the management team led by interim CEO Colette Kress is working to stabilize operations and prepare for the quarterly earnings report to be released on Tuesday.

This episode reflects the multi-sided maneuvering over governance and government-business relations at the leading AI compute company, and the direction of its leadership may affect market expectations for Nvidia and the AI industry chain.
